text:
Maria Chen: FYI escalated from Acme Labs — p99 latency jumped to 1.8s this morning, customer says requests pinned to us-east are hitting eu-west unexpectedly
Sanjay Patel: Can you paste the trace id? also which host/region are they pinned to?
Maria Chen: Trace: https://traces.redwood.dev/trace/ff12ab34
Maria Chen: They set header `x-redwood-region: us-east-1` and the account is on a dedicated pool in us-east
Elaine Kim: I looked at the trace — I see: handler@us-east -> egress-gw.eu-west-1 -> final. Something is rewriting/redirecting the egress path
Kevin O'Rourke: Did the customer's VPC NAT change? that would change their egress IP and our region routing might favor the nearest region
Maria Chen: Customer mentioned they rotated their NAT last night; their DNS TTL is 300 but our logs show cached mapping for ~24h :thinking:
ops-bot: alert: egress-ip-change detected for acct-acme (ip 34.112.55.77 -> 35.198.11.9) at 1900456900
Sanjay Patel: Repro steps for support: from a host with their egress IP run `curl -v -H 'x-redwood-region: us-east-1' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -D -` and check which LB you TLS to
Sanjay Patel: When I run that against 35.198.11.9 it performs TLS handshake with eu-west LB cert
Maria Chen: Added traceroute snippet from their box: ```traceroute to api.redwood.dev (35.198.11.9), 30 hops max
 10  10.1.2.1  5.2 ms 5.1 ms 5.0 ms
 14  35.198.11.9  90.4 ms``` — exit path clearly heads to eu
Elaine Kim: Hypothesis: the new egress IP maps to a provider-owned IP block that our geo-ip->region mapping classifies as eu-west. Need to refresh IP->region mapping service and check cache TTLs
Kevin O'Rourke: Action items: 1) short-term: add per-account egress override for Acme to force us-east routing. 2) mid-term: refresh provider IP geolocation feed and reduce cache TTL for mapping. 3) audit DNS resolver caching between control plane and edge
Maria Chen: Opening an incident for the account and notifying the customer. They asked about credits due to added latency/billing impact
Sanjay Patel: There's a mapping patch in PR #4420 to refresh feed handling, but won't ship until tomorrow. Applying temporary mapping via console now
Maria Chen: I'll message the customer with repro steps and ETA. :thumbsup:
Kevin O'Rourke: Follow-up: add an alert when traces for pinned-region accounts show cross-region hops (so we catch regressions fast) :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Elaine Kim: Also adding a runbook snippet: how to collect `tcpdump -w` and `curl -v` from their egress, and how to set the override from the console
Maria Chen: Closing loop once override applied and p99 returns to baseline.
